correctness.rationale: For each nonzero sign word, exact indicator expansion over F_q removes five zero-entry starts. All five singleton sums vanish, all ten distinct pair sums equal -1, higher subset sums (degrees 3,4,5) are squarefree and each obeys the classical (degree−1) sqrt(q) Weil bound, hence 32*N>=q−39*sqrt(q)−90>0 for q>=1697. The fifteen and only fifteen eligible smaller nonprime prime powers are exactly enumerated by the embedded standard-library verify.py. It constructs each field using proven irreducible polynomials, enumerates every element, cross-checks all quadratic characters against Euler criterion and degree-two norm, and checks all 32 cells and zero-avoidance. All finite cases passed; no finite test substitutes for the large-field proof. Primary proof and exact checker were reconstructed and run.

originality.rationale: The verified 2024 Cohen paper treats homogeneous triples and special quadruples in finite fields, not all mixed five-letter words. The 2023 Wang–Fang paper and 2026 Buchaev–Tsfasman abstract address prime-field sequences, not this nonprime-field complete list. A published prime-field six-letter classification and an accessible four-letter nonprime classification have distinct domains or lengths and do not imply five-letter coverage. No matching full exception classification appeared in eight actual published-finding corpus searches or accessible own claim comparisons. This is best-knowledge originality subject to residual general-curve-formula/unindexed-table risk.
residual_risks: The full arXiv 2026 Buchaev–Tsfasman paper could not be inspected; its general formulas may imply extension-field cases indirectly despite prime-field abstract scope.
A generic character-sum or curve-trace database might permit computing the same classification, and an unindexed table might predate this result.
The finite certificate is executed within one environment; no independent human or independent tool-chain verification has been performed.

value.rationale: Complete exact existence classification of a natural five-shift character-distribution invariant on an infinite and structurally important class of finite fields. All five exceptional field orders and every missing word are enumerated, distinguishing quadratic, cubic and quartic extensions; sharp threshold 289 is not implied by known shorter-pattern or prime-field results. This is a motivated classification beyond a routine example, without asserting a general word-length theory.
